full_original_page:
# 929. A uniform bilinear square-function bound for arbitrary sharp strips

**Area:** Harmonic analysis and bilinear Fourier multipliers
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

Fix $`2<p_1,p_2<\infty`$ and $`1<p<2`$ with $`1/p=1/p_1+1/p_2`$. For a finite family $`\Omega`$ of pairwise disjoint bounded open intervals of positive length, define

```math
\pi_\omega(f,g)(x)=\iint_{\mathbb R^2}
\widehat f(\xi)\widehat g(\eta)\mathbf1_\omega(\xi-\eta)
e^{2\pi i x(\xi+\eta)}\,d\xi\,d\eta,
\qquad \omega\in\Omega,
```

using $`\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\xi}\,dx`$.

Does there exist $`C_{p_1,p_2}<\infty`$, independent of the family, such that every pair of complex Schwartz functions satisfies

```math
\left\|\left(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}|\pi_\omega(f,g)|^2\right)^{1/2}\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb R)}
\le C_{p_1,p_2}\|f\|_{L^{p_1}(\mathbb R)}\|g\|_{L^{p_2}(\mathbb R)}?
```

Widths and separations are arbitrary. The cutoffs are characteristic functions of the diagonal strips $`\{(\xi,\eta):\xi-\eta\in\omega\}`$.

## Application

This asks whether disjoint frequency-difference bands yield a uniform square-function estimate despite the modulation invariance of their bilinear Hilbert-transform geometry.

## References

1. F. Bernicot and M. Vitturi, [A bilinear Rubio de Francia inequality for arbitrary rectangles](https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnz177), *International Mathematics Research Notices* **2021**(17), 12925–12966. [Archived manuscript](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.06534v1), introduction, printed p.2, sharp-strip formula and arbitrary-strip question.
2. F. Bernicot, [On the boundedness for the bilinear quadratic functional given by arbitrary strips](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.22134v1) (2026), Theorem1.1 and Remark1.5(c).

## Status review


**Known cases:** Sharp characteristic cutoffs for arbitrary disjoint diagonal strips are essential. The June 2026 smooth-cutoff estimate with a cardinality epsilon loss explicitly leaves this assertion separate; equal-width and axis-aligned rectangle estimates do not settle it.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.

The equal-width result in [1] covers this strict local-L2 exponent range. Removing that geometry is the question.
